item.content:encoded:

🗓
On November 9
, the international round table "
Militarization of Europe: What next?
" was held in Vienna, organized by the
Delegation of the Russian Federation to the Vienna Negotiations on Military Security and Arms Control
.
The event focused on analyzing
the current situation in Europe, marked by the unprecedented militarization
under the pretext of countering the "Russian threat".
#NATO
and the
#EU
are openly preparing for war against Russia
, predicting that it could break out within the next 3–5 years.
Participants discussed
the consequences of the massive increase in mil spending
by European countries, the
expansion of military infrastructure
in "frontline states" bordering Russia, and
NATO's provocative plans
against our country.
❗️
In 2025, military spending by NATO states already amounted to ~ $1.6 trln. In 2025, spending by the 27 EU states reached EUR 418 bln and is projected to rise to EUR 800 bln by 2030.
❗️
💊
Particular emphasis was placed on the
harmful effects of the intensive information and propaganda campaign
conducted by European countries to condition their own populations to accept the idea of an "inevitable" conflict with Russia.
The "Russian threat" is used to justify everything citizens are expected to sacrifice
in the struggle against our country. The increase in European military spending is taking place against a backdrop of
economic stagnation and will have serious social consequences.
💊
An important topic of discussion was the existing mechanisms for
de-escalation
, including those between Russia and NATO. It was noted that their use has become increasingly difficult, while bilateral de-escalation channels remain virtually frozen, including dialogue under
agreements on the prevention of incidents on and over the high seas, as well as on the prevention of dangerous military activities
.
💊
Special attention was paid to the Ukrainian crisis and its connection with European militarization.
Ukraine is being systematically integrated into the defense industries of European countries, while the battlefield experience of the Armed Forces of Ukraine is being used
to prepare for a conflict with our country.
The round table opened with a
video address by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation S.A. Ryabkov
. The event brought together representatives of the Vienna diplomatic corps, international and regional organizations, including the UN and the OSCE, as well as prominent experts and journalists.
🎙
Speakers at the round table included
:
- Head of a Division of the Department of International Military Cooperation of the MoD of the Republic of Belarus Lieutenant Colonel
E.Rusak
;
- Deputy Director of the Department for Non-Proliferation and Arms Control of the Russian MFA
A.Mazur
;
- Head of a Division of the 2nd CIS Department of the Russian MFA
A.Postigov
;
- Vice-Rector for International Relations and Security of the Russian State Academy of Intellectual Property, Reserve Colonel
A.Likhonosov
;
- Professor Emeritus of Political Science at Columbia University,
Dr. Robert Legvold
;
- Austrian political scientist and journalist
D.Reinisch
;
- Associate Professor at the Department of Political Philosophy and Geopolitics at Uni Dolomiti in Belluno, Italy,
L.M.Pacini
.
☝️
Following the round table,
we reiterate that Russia does not seek confrontation with NATO and does not want war with Europe
. European countries must abandon their dangerous course, which gives them the illusion of protection against external threats but will, in reality, lead to catastrophic consequences.

⚡
Article
by Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation Sergey Lavrov, The Impact of Global Economy on International Security
(based on remarks at
the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
on October 30-31, 2026)
✍️
A meeting of
G20 Foreign Ministers took place
in the United States not long ago. The participants focused on the global economy and its interconnection and interdependence with international security.
I offered a number of assessments in
my remarks at the meeting that I would like to share
with a wider readership.
Key points:
👉
Geopolitical Context
• In an ideal world, the global economy and international security
should complement each other
and jointly provide a foundation for peaceful coexistence and shared prosperity. Instead, the economy is increasingly becoming
an arena of confrontation, with trade wars being unleashed
to suppress geopolitical competitors in the wake of hot wars.
• The objective process of the emergence of a multipolar world order is being met with outright hostility in the West. <...>
Protectionist barriers
, and even outright blockades, in the way of the dissemination of
advanced technologies
are multiplying.
• The European Union, which is turning itself into a military bloc <...> has harked back to the days of
slavery
and
piracy
and taken to openly seizing foreign vessels and stealing their cargoes. T
o justify this plunder
, it has invented the term
“shadow fleet,”
which has no basis in international law.
👉
All these actions by the West are in direct violation of international law. They create uncertainty and additional costs, and undermine global economic connectivity and long-term resilience. In effect,
they are dismantling the very globalisation model
that the West itself created and promoted for decades as the ideal system of global economic governance, a kind of
“economic end of history.”
👉
Global energy and food security
• A stable global energy system is an essential prerequisite for sustained economic growth and the adoption of innovative technologies. <...> However,
the normal functioning of energy markets is being undermined
by a number of factors.
• Feeling emboldened by the EU’s unconditional support,
the Kiev regime has come to believe that it can act with impunity
carrying out terrorist attacks against critical infrastructure.
• US President
Donald Trump’s calls on Ukraine
to stop fuelling the energy crisis
have been ignored
.
❗️
To this day, those who organised the acts of sabotage against
the Nord Stream pipelines
mentioned above have not been brought to justice.
•
The aggression against Iran
, which led to
the closure of the Strait of Hormuz
, was a serious destabilising factor that has dealt a severe blow to the energy sector.
•
Food security
is another important component of global security. <...> This year, G20 trade ministers
condemned the weaponisation of food supplies
👉
What is needed now is
to translate words into concrete action
.
👉
Russia in the global economy: A constructive contribution despite challenges
• The illegitimate sanctions have inflicted losses running into trillions on Europe,
fuelled inflation in the United States
, and reduced living standards in many countries
(hence the surge in protest sentiment across the European Union)
.
• Russia will continue to contribute to normalising global fuel and energy markets. <...> We are among the leading exporters of hydrocarbons to Asia, Africa, and Latin America.
***
We are convinced that
the future lies in the democratisation of international economic relations
and the restructuring of the global economy on a genuinely multipolar basis. Global markets and supply chains must be open, competitive, and inclusive, while trade and investment cooperation must be based on equality and predictability. <...>
For its part, Russia and its partners and like-minded countries, primarily within BRICS, the SCO, the EAEU, and the CIS, will continue working to advance a constructive agenda aimed at
building a fairer and more prosperous world for all countries without exception
.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33276

🎙
Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
answer to a media question
at a joint news conference with Peru’s Foreign Minister Carlos Espa
(Moscow, November 9, 2026)
❓
Question: What are your expectations for the upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi? Speaking about the talks earlier, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the conflict would have to be resolved before discussions could begin on security guarantees for Ukraine and Europe. We noticed that the Russian delegation has been expanded this time to include Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov. Does this mean there will be a separate negotiating track?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
I heard US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio’s
remarks
about the growing importance of security issues, both at the Abu Dhabi talks and in the broader context of the Ukraine conflict.
In fact, the first item on the agenda in Abu Dhabi is
the security of Russia, Ukraine and the region as a whole
. We can only welcome this approach.
Let me remind you what we did to avert what would otherwise have been inevitable.
We know what plans the Kiev regime was making in late 2021 and early 2022
to resolve the Donbass issue by force. In December 2021, acting on instructions from President Vladimir Putin,
we presented the US and NATO members with
two draft treaties
aimed at strengthening the foundations of equal and indivisible security.
Several meetings followed
. A Russian interagency delegation met with our NATO counterparts.
I then met in Geneva with Antony Blinken
, who was US Secretary of State at the time. We explained to him in detail why
it was essential to do everything in our power to put the principles of indivisible security into practice
. These principles had been proclaimed loud and clear at the highest level of the OSCE,
👉
yet they were being swept under the carpet
.
One of them states that
no organisation in the Euro-Atlantic area has the right to claim military and political dominance
. NATO was doing precisely the opposite.
That principle was endorsed
as far back as 1999 at
the Istanbul Summit
and reaffirmed in 2010 at
the Astana Summit
.
After
the talks
between the Russian and US delegations, during which we pressed these points,
Antony Blinken
asked to speak to me in private.
He told me we would get nowhere
. The US had already made its decision, he said. By then, the Americans
had withdrawn
from
the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty
and were preparing to deploy these missiles in various parts of the world.
☝️
Antony Blinken said the only assurance they could give us was that there might be limits on the deployment in Ukraine of intermediate- and shorter-range missiles aimed at Russia
. As for a guarantee that Ukraine would stay out of NATO, he said that was out of the question. They would never make such a promise.
In other words,
the administration of then US President Joe Biden could not have cared less about “European security”
, particularly the security of Russia, which is our primary concern.
We can only welcome the fact that the current US negotiators, acting on instructions from President
Donald Trump
, have proposed
putting collective security at the top of the agenda
for the talks on a settlement in Ukraine.
👉
Everyone understands that the purpose of these talks is
to agree on the principles to be endorsed at the conclusion of negotiations on a comprehensive settlement
.
It is entirely natural that another of my deputies,
Sergey Ryabkov
, should join
Mikhail Galuzin
in the delegation. His responsibilities cover
North Atlantic affairs
and
arms control
in the broadest sense. He has also spent a considerable part of his career working on
OSCE matters
.

📆
On November 9,
the Russia National Centre
hosted the 14th Meeting of Secretaries of the Security Councils of the
#CIS
Member States.
Secretary of Russia’s Security Council
Sergey Shoigu
chaired the meeting.
✉️
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
sent
a message of greetings
to the participants:
Today, with the geopolitical situation complex and conflicts intensifying in several regions of the world, it is important to make full use of your councils’ considerable capacity for analysis and forecasting to strengthen the security and sovereignty of the
#CIS
Member States and maintain stability throughout the Commonwealth.
🤝
The participants discussed
current security challenges and threats across the CIS
and
joint measures
they could take to address them. They also reviewed the outcomes of
the Peoples of Russia International Week
.
💬
Secretary of Russia’s Security Council
Sergey Shoigu
:
The countries of the Global South and East are playing an increasingly influential role in world politics and the global economy, shaping the course of international relations and the contours of the security architecture. In the current circumstances, it is important to work together to put mechanisms in place so that we are ready to deal with the consequences of international crises as they arise.
Russia has proposed that
#BRICS
and the
#SCO
establish emergency stockpiles to help people in partner countries in the event of an emergency.
The proposal is to establish regional hubs at key points in the logistics network to hold vital reserves, primarily food and energy supplies, critical materials, medicines and other essential goods.
©️
📸
Press Service of the Russia National Centre

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at talks with Peru’s Foreign Minister Carlos Espa
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at talks with Peru’s Foreign Minister Carlos Espa (Moscow, November 9, 2026) 💬 Sergey Lavrov: We are glad to welcome you. I am particularly pleased to meet you in person, Mr Minister. We attach great importance to your visit. This is the first time in many years that the Foreign Ministers of Russia and Peru have met in person. We have great respect for Peruvian diplomacy , which draws on the knowledge and experience your country has gained over the millennia. Like Russia, Peru is a unique civilisation shaped by many peoples and cultures . People in Russia know your country well and appreciate its distinctive traditions, music and cuisine. Relations between our countries go back almost 165 years . July 18 has become an unofficial day of Russian-Peruvian solidarity. On that day in 1970, Soviet medical personnel were on their way to help Peru after a devastating earthquake when they lost their lives in a plane crash over the Atlantic . We are grateful to the people of Peru for honouring their memory. 🤝 Your visit to Moscow today on behalf of President Keiko Fujimori gives us a good opportunity to review the full range of our bilateral relations and exchange views on international and regional issues , as well as on our cooperation at the UN and in other international organisations. 🇷🇺 🇵🇪 #RussiaPeru
